data.title: Tempest Therapeutics Reports Q3 2026 Results, $0.9 Million Cash Balance
data.description:
Tempest Therapeutics reported a third-quarter 2026 net loss of $3.6 million, or $0.21 per share, and ended September with $0.9 million in cash. The company said its cash is expected to fund operating expenses for less than 12 months from the date its financial statements were available to be issued, raising substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern. The quarter’s business update included an exclusive license for Senlang’s CD7-targeted lentiviral in vivo CAR-T platform.

Financial Highlights

  • Third-quarter net loss was $3.6 million, compared with $3.5 million in the year-earlier quarter; net loss per share was $0.21, versus $0.79.
  • For the first nine months of 2026, net loss was $36.6 million, or $2.54 per share, compared with $22.2 million, or $5.71 per share, in the same period of 2025.
  • Cash and cash equivalents totaled $0.9 million at September 30, 2026, down from $7.7 million at December 31, 2025. Cash used in operating activities during the first nine months was $12.4 million.
  • Third-quarter research and development expenses were $0.2 million and general and administrative expenses were $2.6 million. For the first nine months, those expenses were $2.1 million and $11.5 million, respectively, with acquired in-process research and development expenses of $22.2 million.
  • Tempest recorded $0.8 million in third-quarter financing costs related to its Lincoln Park equity line. It also reported approximately $1.8 million in net proceeds from its September private placement and approximately $0.3 million in gross proceeds from Lincoln Park share sales through September 30.

Business Highlights

  • Tempest exercised its option to obtain an exclusive worldwide license, excluding China, to Senlang’s CD7-targeted lentiviral vector platform and associated in vivo CAR-T candidates.
  • Lead candidate TPST-4903, a BCMA/GPRC5D dual-targeting in vivo CAR-T therapy, is being evaluated in a Phase 1 dose-escalation study for relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma. The company said preliminary clinical responses were encouraging and that initial data are expected at an upcoming scientific conference.
  • Tempest highlighted TPST-4003, a CD19/BCMA dual-targeting candidate using its CD7-targeted mRNA/LNP delivery platform. An investigator-initiated study in China involving approximately 10 patients with myasthenia gravis or multiple sclerosis is expected to begin in the fourth quarter of 2026.
  • The company appointed Nancy Freda-Smith and John W. Frederick as independent directors, citing their corporate governance and capital markets expertise.

Original SEC Filing: Tempest Therapeutics, Inc. [ TPST ] - 8-K - Nov. 13, 2026

data.title: Mistras Group Supplements Merger Proxy Amid Stockholder Lawsuits
data.description:

  • The supplement does not change the merger terms or November 24 special meeting date, and the board continues to recommend a vote in favor.

data.title: MacroGenics Updates Clinical Pipeline, Reports $288M in Cash and Runway Through 2028
data.description:

Key Highlights:

  • MGC026’s SCCHN cohort showed a 27.3% best overall response rate and 63.6% disease control rate among 22 patients.

data.title: BeyondSpring Reports $50.5 Million Q3 Net Income, Advances DUBLIN-4
data.description:
BeyondSpring reported third-quarter 2026 net income of $50.5 million, largely reflecting a $53.7 million gain on the sale of subsidiary interests, while its continuing operations recorded a $2.1 million net loss. The company reported no revenue and a $2.1 million operating loss for the quarter. Business updates included FDA Fast Track designation for Plinabulin plus docetaxel and a transaction to support China-based enrollment in the DUBLIN-4 trial.

Financial Highlights

  • Revenue was $0 for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026.
  • Operating loss from continuing operations was $2.1 million for the third quarter, compared with $1.6 million a year earlier; the nine-month operating loss was $5.7 million, versus $5.9 million.
  • Net income was $50.5 million for the third quarter, including a $53.7 million gain on the sale of subsidiary interests. Net income attributable to BeyondSpring was $50.8 million.
  • For the nine months, net income was $38.1 million, including the sale gain; net income attributable to BeyondSpring was $47.8 million.
  • Basic and diluted earnings per share were $1.24 for the quarter, including a $0.05 loss per share from continuing operations. Cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments totaled $0.6 million at September 30, 2026, compared with $4.0 million at December 31, 2025.

Business Highlights

  • The FDA granted Fast Track designation to Plinabulin plus docetaxel for advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC without actionable genomic alterations after anti-PD-(L)1 therapy and platinum-based chemotherapy. The designation may allow more frequent FDA interactions and, if criteria are met, rolling review.
  • BeyondSpring completed the sale of BeyondSpring Ltd., which indirectly held a majority equity interest in Bulin, to Biolin on September 30, 2026. Under the transaction, Biolin will support Bulin’s DUBLIN-4 clinical development activities at participating sites in China, with enrollment expected to include approximately 221 patients.
  • BeyondSpring will have access to clinical data from the China portion of DUBLIN-4. The global Phase 3 trial plans to enroll 442 patients, with a prespecified interim analysis at 221 progression-free survival events.
  • The company cited DUBLIN-3 results and a post-ICI subgroup analysis, along with prospective Phase 2 Study 303 data presented at ASCO 2026, as clinical rationale for evaluating Plinabulin in the post-ICI setting.

Original SEC Filing: BeyondSpring Inc. [ BYSI ] - 8-K - Nov. 13, 2026

data.title: BCP Investment reports Q3 loss, $13.13 NAV per share and proposed ICMB merger
data.description:
BCP Investment reported third-quarter 2026 net investment income of $4.6 million, or $0.37 per share, and a net decrease in assets from operations of $13.5 million. Net asset value was $162.7 million, or $13.13 per share, at September 30. The company also agreed to acquire Investcorp Credit Management BDC at consideration equal to 90% of its adjusted net asset value.

Financial Highlights

  • Total investment income was $13.9 million, down from $18.9 million in the third quarter of 2025. Core investment income, excluding purchase discount accretion, was $12.2 million.
  • Net investment income was $4.6 million, or $0.37 per share, compared with $8.8 million, or $0.71 per share, a year earlier.
  • The net decrease in assets resulting from operations was $13.5 million, or $1.09 per share, versus a $23.6 million increase, or $1.88 per share, in the prior-year quarter.
  • Net asset value was $162.7 million, or $13.13 per share, compared with $179.5 million, or $14.49 per share, at June 30, 2026.
  • At quarter-end, investments had a fair value of $434.2 million. Outstanding borrowings were $282.4 million at par, and the asset coverage ratio was approximately 157%.

Business Highlights

  • BCP Investment entered into a merger agreement to acquire Investcorp Credit Management BDC. ICMB shareholders will receive newly issued BCP Investment shares and, if applicable, cash, based on consideration equal to 90% of ICMB’s adjusted net asset value. The transaction is subject to customary closing conditions, including ICMB shareholder approval.
  • During the quarter, the company deployed approximately $3.1 million and received approximately $8.9 million from repayments and sales, resulting in net repayments and sales of approximately $5.8 million.
  • Non-accrual debt investments declined to 10 across seven portfolio companies, from 11 across seven companies in the prior quarter. They represented 2.8% of the portfolio’s fair value and 6.0% of amortized cost.
  • BCP Investment amended its KeyBank revolving credit facility, increasing committed capacity to $150 million, lowering borrowing spreads, and extending the reinvestment period to August 2029 and maturity to August 2031. The amendment consolidated secured revolving borrowings after the JPMorgan facility was repaid and terminated.
  • The company issued an additional $10 million of 7.50% notes due 2029 and redeemed its remaining $10 million of 2026 Notes in October, eliminating that near-term maturity.
  • BCP Investment declared monthly base distributions of $0.09 per share for January, February and March 2027.

data.title: Grades steady as global oil markets set to return to surplus
data.description:
Grades were little changed on Friday, dealers said, even as global oil market was set to return to a surplus in the fourth quarter of this year, according to the International Energy Agency.

Oil supply will average 105 million barrels per day in the fourth quarter, the Paris-based agency, which advises industrialized countries, said in a monthly report, 1.7 million bpd higher than forecast demand. The IEA had previously forecast a fourth-quarter supply deficit.

Iraq, OPEC's second-largest producer, has been working to find alternative export routes for its oil since the Strait of Hormuz, its usual outlet, was disrupted by the Iran war. The country has been shipping oil on hundreds of tankers to the Syrian port of Baniyas via an overland desert route which had been largely unused for decades.

In the US, President Donald Trump extended for 90 days a waiver of a shipping law to allow foreign-flagged ships to transport oil and other commodities between US ports, a White House official said on Friday.

Oil rig counts, an indicator of future supply, was unchanged at 463 this week.

  • Light Louisiana Sweet (WTC-LLS) for December delivery firmed 5 cents to a midpoint of a $1.90 premium and was seen bid and offered between a $1.80 and $2.00 a barrel premium to U.S. crude futures ​

  • Mars Sour (WTC-MRS) was unchanged at a midpoint of a $3.5 discount and was seen bid and offered between a $3.75 and $3.25 a barrel discount to U.S. crude futures ​

  • WTI Midland (WTC-WTM)was unchanged at a midpoint of a 20-cent premium and was seen bid and offered between parity and 40-cent​ a barrel premium to U.S. crude futures ​

  • West Texas Sour (WTC-WTS) was flat at a midpoint of a $3.3 discount and was seen bid and offered between a $3.50 and $3.10 a barrel discount to U.S. crude futures ​

  • WTI at East Houston (WTC-MEH), also known as MEH, traded between a 60-cent and 90-cent a barrel premium to U.S. crude futures ​

  • ICE Brent January futures rose 2 cents to settle at $95.84 a barrel on Friday​.

  • WTI December crude futures fell 18 cents to settle at $88.56 a barrel on Friday​.

  • The Brent/WTI spread (WTCLc1-LCOc1) widened 36 cents to to last trade at minus $8.49, after hitting a high of minus $8.01 and a low of minus $8.74.

data.title: Japan Display narrows first-half net loss after restructuring
data.description:
Japan Display Inc. , the Japanese maker of small and mid-sized liquid crystal display panels, cut its net loss to JPY7.04bn ($44mn) for the six months to September, Jiji Press reported on November 13. A year earlier, the company lost JPY11.36bn over the same period.

The figures arrive months after JDI removed the threat of delisting. The panel maker had liabilities exceeding its assets at the end of March 2026. Had that position continued to the end of March 2027, the company risked breaching Tokyo Stock Exchange listing rules. JDI cleared the shortfall by the end of June. By the end of September its net assets stood at a positive JPY5bn, against a negative net worth of JPY7.41bn six months before.

Restructuring carried out in the previous fiscal year narrowed the loss, the company said. That included reducing its workforce. Paying down debt also brought interest costs lower.

Revenue moved the other way. Group sales for the half year declined 33.1% to JPY44.48bn. The company linked the decline to the end of output at its Mobara factory in Chiba Prefecture, according to results JDI published on November 12.

'Major structural reforms have reached a milestone,' JDI President Jun Akema said at a briefing on the earnings.

He said the company's attention would now turn to generating profit from the overhaul.

'Our top priority is to steadily translate these efforts into earnings and return to profitability as soon as possible,' Akema said.

data.title: Japan's Watami considers management buyout to delist
data.description:
Watami Co. , the Japanese operator of izakaya pubs, is weighing a management buyout that would take it off the stock market, Jiji Press reported on November 13, citing people with knowledge of the plan.

The company wants to give its executives more room to manoeuvre as it tries to reduce its reliance on Japanese-style pubs. Drinking is declining among consumers, and young people in particular are turning away from alcohol.

An asset management firm belonging to Miki Watanabe, who founded the restaurant group and serves as its chairman and chief executive, is expected to launch a tender offer for Watami's shares shortly, the sources said.

Watami has been building up businesses outside its pub chain. In 2024 it bought the Japanese operations of sandwich chain Subway, and it also runs boxed meal delivery services.

data.title: Inovalis Real Estate Investment Trust Announces the Financial Results for Q3 2026
data.description:
Inovalis Real Estate Investment Trust (the “REIT”) (TSX: INO.UN) today reported financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. The unaudited Consolidated Financial Statements and Management’s Discussion and Analysis (“MD&A”) for Q3 2026 and 2025 are available on the REIT’s website at www.inovalisreit.com and at www.sedarplus.ca. All amounts except rental rates, square footage and per unit amounts are presented in thousands of Canadian dollars or Euros, or as otherwise stated.

Stephane Amine, CEO and President of the REIT, commented “During the quarter, management continued to advance several key transactions, engage with lenders on financing arrangements and address operational priorities across the portfolio. While these initiatives take time to conclude, they remain important to our efforts to manage debt obligations, address property-level challenges and maintain financial flexibility in a difficult operating environment”.

Net Rental Income

For the portfolio that includes assets owned entirely by the REIT (“IP Portfolio”), Q3 2026 Net Rental Income (“NRI”) was $2,861 (€1,779) compared to $3,701 (€2,367) for Q3 2025. The decrease was primarily attributable to the sale of the Trio property in January 2026 as the property was 73% leased until December 2025. The negative impact of the Trio sale was partially offset by the absence in 2026 of the Baldi property, which was vacant and made a negative contribution to NRI in Q3 2025 prior to its disposition in December 2025.

In Q3 2026, NRI, adjusted for IFRIC 21 for the portfolio that includes the REIT's proportionate share in joint ventures (“Total Portfolio”), was $4,229 (€2,630), in decrease compared to $5,101 (€3,263) for Q3 2025. The decrease reflects the above factors on the IP Portfolio and a $118 decrease in the REIT's share of joint venture NRI ($2,234 compared to $2,352 for Q3 2025). For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the REIT's share of joint venture NRI increased by $471, notably reflecting the leasing of 20% vacant space in the Neu-Isenburg property since Q4 2025.

Leasing Operations

As of September 30, 2026, the REIT’s IP Portfolio occupancy was 38.2%, and 55.7% for the REIT's Total Portfolio. Strategic vacancy continues to be maintained in the Arcueil and Delizy properties in support of the dispositions which, for both properties, are currently under exchange contracts as outlined in the Asset Recycling Plan. Excluding Arcueil and Delizy, the Total Portfolio occupancy rate was 82% at September 30, 2026.

On the Metropolitain property, a 6-year firm extension was signed over 18,800 sq. ft. office space, improving the property's WALT from 5.4 to 6.7 years (WALB from 3.2 to 3.8 years).

Prospective tenants have been identified, particularly for the Bad Homburg property. If these leasing opportunities result in executed leases, occupancy at the property and across the portfolio could increase significantly.

Asset Recycling Plan

The REIT is progressing toward the Q1 2027 closing of the sale of 87.5% of the Arcueil property for $60,537 (€37,540) which is conditional upon the issuance of a building permit. The building permit was obtained subsequent to quarter-end, in November 2026, triggering a customary period for the expiry of appeal rights. Marketing efforts are ongoing for the remaining 12.5% interest in the property which is dedicated to office tenants.

Preliminary exchange contract for the Delizy property

During Q3, on July 28, 2026, the REIT signed preliminary exchange contracts with three developers for the disposition of the Delizy property located in the north of Paris at a sale price of $28,067 (€17,405). The transaction is anticipated to close in Q3 2027 to provide time to address sale conditions. The transaction is subject to building permit approval and eviction of the remaining tenants at the REIT’s expense estimated to be $2,200. Net proceeds are expected to be used to repay the senior lender.

Book Value and Realizable Value

As the REIT continues to dispose of properties individually under its Asset Recycling Plan, readers should note the following regarding book value per Unit. Book value per Unit is derived from the REIT’s IFRS carrying values. The fair value of the REIT’s investment properties is supported by external appraisals as at June 30, 2026, reviewed by management as at September 30, 2026, which estimate the value of each property individually, assuming an orderly transaction between market participants under normal market conditions. Book value per Unit is not an estimate of the amount that would be realized on a sale of the REIT’s properties or of the REIT, or of the amount that would be available for distribution to Unitholders, and readers should consider it with caution. Amounts that may ultimately be realized are forward-looking information and could be materially lower than book value as a result of, among other things: (i) social tensions in France, which may disrupt property operations and reduce tenant demand and investor appetite; (ii) continuing political uncertainty in France, including the absence of a stable majority government and its potential effect on lending and investment activity, fiscal policy and France’s sovereign credit rating; (iii) the ongoing costs borne by the REIT while properties are sold individually over an extended period, including debt service, property operating and vacancy costs, eviction and capital expenditure costs, general and administrative expenses, and transaction costs and taxes, which reduce the net cash available to the REIT from each disposition; (iv) material refinancing risk, as a significant portion of the REIT’s debt matures within the next 12 months and lenders may require deleveraging, impose less favourable terms or decline to extend or refinance; (v) the structure of the REIT’s financing, including asset-level, non-recourse debt under which the REIT may realize little or no equity value from a property whose value is less than the debt secured on it, and arrangements under which proceeds from the sale of one property may be required to be applied to debt secured on other properties; and (vi) interest rates, including recent increases in European Central Bank policy rates and the REIT’s exposure to variable-rate debt, which may increase capitalization rates and reduce property values. The Units have traded at a significant discount to book value per Unit; the closing price of the Units on the Toronto Stock Exchange was $0.69 on September 30, 2026. See “Forward-Looking Information” below and “Risks and Uncertainties” in the MD&A.

Capital Market Considerations

European real estate markets continued to face a challenging operating environment in Q3 2026. Renewed inflationary pressures and the resulting increases in European Central Bank policy rates in June and September 2026, higher financing costs relative to prior cycles, limited market liquidity, and ongoing geopolitical uncertainty continued to weigh on investment activity and asset valuations.

Unitholders’ equity was $139,683 (€86,620) as at September 30, 2026. Book value per Unit was $4.17 ($4.13 fully diluted).

In the current market, the REIT remains focused on a balanced debt and cash structure. At September 30, 2026, debt to gross book value, net of cash, was 59.8% for the Total Portfolio and 50.1% for the IP Portfolio.

Management continues to evaluate capital allocation decisions through the lens of value per transaction and sustainable leverage reduction.

Liquidity and Capital Position

As at September 30, 2026, REIT’s cash position (excluding restricted cash) was $12,537 compared to $25,057 as at December 31, 2025. Available liquidity is expected to be used to service senior debt including interest and amortization, fund tenant improvements to advance leasing activity, and address tax-related obligations, subject to the outcome of an ongoing appeal.

In addition to available cash, the REIT held $1,289 in restricted cash at September 30, 2026, which may be applied toward partial deleveraging in advance of loan extensions or upon property dispositions. The REIT also held $4,207 of cash within assets held in joint venture, including $1,709 of restricted cash established in connection with debt refinancing intended to support lender requirements, capital expenditures and leasing incentives. In September, $1,970 (€1,222) of the restricted cash was allocated to debt, pursuant to the mortgage loan extension of the Kosching property.

Funds From Operations and Adjusted Funds From Operations1

In the calculation of FFO for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, $17,020 in non-recurring finance income recognized in Q1 2026 in relation to the Trio disposition has been excluded. FFO and AFFO per Unit for Q3 2026 were $0.00 and $(0.01) respectively, reflecting the current occupancy level and borrowing costs.

Refer to the “Non-GAAP Financial Measures and Other Measures” section of this MD&A for a more detailed discussion on FFO and AFFO.

Financing Activity

The REIT is financed almost exclusively with asset-level, non-recourse financing with an average term to maturity of 1.8 years for the IP Portfolio (1.6 years for the Total Portfolio).

Management continues to execute its broader financing strategy, which includes a combination of asset dispositions, debt repayment and refinancing initiatives. A number of mortgage facilities mature over the next 12 months, and management is actively engaged with its lending partners to extend or refinance these facilities on commercially reasonable terms while minimizing deleveraging requirements.

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the weighted average interest rate across the Total Portfolio was 3.95%. As at September 30, 2026, 63% of the REIT's Total Portfolio debt was subject to variable interest rates, primarily associated with short-term financing or on properties currently being marketed for sale.

FORWARD-LOOKING INFORMATION

Forward-looking information may relate to the REIT's future outlook and anticipated events or results and may include statements regarding the future financial position, business strategy, budgets, occupancy rates, rental rates, productivity, projected costs, capital investments, development and development opportunities, financial results, taxes, plans and objectives of or involving the REIT. Particularly, statements regarding the REIT’s future results, performance, achievements, prospects, costs, opportunities, and financial outlook, including those relating to the sale of the Arcueil property, acquisition and capital investment strategies and the real estate industry generally, are forward-looking statements. In some cases, forward-looking information can be identified by terms such as “may”, “will”, “should”, “expect”, “plan”, “anticipate”, “believe”, “intend”, “estimate”, “predict”, “potential”, “continue” or the negative thereof, or other similar expressions concerning matters that are not historical facts. Although management believes that the expectations reflected in the forward-looking information are reasonable, no assurance can be given that these expectations will prove to be correct, and since forward-looking information inherently involves risks and uncertainties, undue reliance should not be placed on such information.

The estimates and assumptions, which may prove to be incorrect, include, but are not limited to, the various assumptions set forth in this press release as well as the following:

  • the ability to obtain an amortization deferral until disposal and to successfully complete the divestment of the Arcueil and Delizy properties;

Non-GAAP Financial Measures and Other Measures

There are financial measures included in this MD&A that do not have a standardized meaning under IFRS. These measures include funds from operations, adjusted funds from operations, and other measures presented on a proportionate share basis. These measures have been derived from the REIT’s financial statements and applied on a consistent basis as appropriate. Management includes these measures as they represent key performance indicators to management, and it believes certain investors use these measures as a means of assessing relative financial performance. These measures, as computed by the REIT, may differ from similar computations as reported by other entities and, accordingly, may not be comparable to other such entities. These measures should not be considered in isolation or used as a substitute for other measures of performance prepared in accordance with IFRS.

USE OF OPERATING METRICS

The REIT uses certain operating metrics to monitor and measure the operational performance of its portfolio. Operating metrics in this press release include GLA, committed occupancy, Weighted Average Lease Term and average term to maturity. Certain of these operating metrics, may constitute supplementary financial measures as defined in National Instrument 52-112 - Non-GAAP and Other Financial Measures Disclosure. These supplementary measures are not derived from directly comparable measures contained in the REIT’s financial statements but may be used by management and disclosed on a periodic basis to depict the historical or future expected financial performance, financial position or cash flow of the REIT.

“Adjusted Funds From Operations” or “AFFO” is a meaningful supplemental measure that can be used to determine the REIT’s ability to service debt, fund expansion capital expenditures, fund property development, and provide distributions to Unitholders after considering costs associated with sustaining operating earnings.

AFFO calculations are reconciled to net income, which is the most directly comparable IFRS measure. AFFO should not be construed as an alternative to net income or cash flow generated from operating activities, determined in accordance with IFRS.

AFFO is defined as FFO subject to certain adjustments, including adjustments for: (i) the non-cash effect of straight-line rents, (ii) the cash effect of the rental guarantee received, (iii) amortization of fair value adjustment on assumed debt, (iv) capital expenditures, excluding those funded by a dedicated cash reserve or capex financing, and (v) amortization of transaction costs on mortgage loans.

“Adjusted Funds From Operations / Unit” or “AFFO / Unit” is AFFO divided by the issued and outstanding Units, plus Exchangeable Securities (fully diluted basis).

“Average loan term to maturity” refers to the average number of years remaining in the financing.

“Book value per Unit” refers to the REIT’s total equity divided by the Weighted Average number of Units and Exchangeable Securities (on a fully diluted basis).

“Debt-service covenant ratio calculation” or “DSCR” refers to the rental income divided by the debt service, including interest and amortization.

“Debt-to-Gross-Book Value” refers to the REIT’s apportioned amount of indebtedness respectively in the IP Portfolio and the Total Portfolio. Indebtedness on an IP and Total Portfolio basis is calculated as the sum of (i) lease liabilities, (ii) mortgage loans, (iii) other long-term liabilities, and (iv) deferred tax liabilities. Indebtedness does not include certain liabilities as is the case for the Exchangeable Securities and at the joint venture level for the contribution from the REIT and its partners.

“Exchangeable Securities” means the exchangeable securities issued by CanCorpEurope, in the form of interest bearing notes, non-interest bearing notes and variable share capital.

“Fully diluted basis” refers to a nominal value divided by the issued and outstanding Units, plus Exchangeable Securities.

“Funds From Operations” or “FFO” 1 follows the definition prescribed by the Real Estate Property Association of Canada publication on Funds From Operations & Adjusted Funds From Operations, dated January 2023 with one exception.

Management considers FFO to be a meaningful supplemental measure that can be used to determine the REIT’s ability to service debt, fund capital expenditures, and provide distributions to Unitholders.

FFO is reconciled to net income, which is the most directly comparable IFRS measure. FFO should not be construed as an alternative to net income or cash flow generated from operating activities, determined in accordance with IFRS.

FFO for the REIT is defined as net income in accordance with IFRS, subject to certain adjustments including adjustments for: (i) acquisition, eviction and disposal costs (if any), (ii) net change in fair value of investment properties, (iii) net change in fair value of derivative financial instruments at fair value through profit and loss, (iv) net changes in fair value of Exchangeable Securities, (v) finance costs related to distribution on Exchangeable Securities, (vi) adjustment for property taxes accounted for under IFRIC 21 (if any), (vii) loss on exercise of lease option (if any), (viii) adjustment for foreign exchange gains or losses on monetary items not forming part of an investment in a foreign operation (if any), (ix) gain or loss on disposal of investment properties or an interest in a subsidiary (if any), (x) finance income earned from loans to joint ventures (if any), (xi) loss on extinguishment of loans (if any), (xii) deferred taxes, (xiii) non-controlling interest, (xiv) goodwill / bargain purchase gains upon acquisition, (xv) income taxes on sale of investment properties and provision for tax reassessment and (xvi) non-recurring finance income related to bank debt waiver correlated with a sale.

Exchangeable Securities are recorded as liabilities. Exchangeable Securities are recorded at fair value through profit and loss in accordance with IFRS. However, both are considered as equity for the purposes of calculating FFO and AFFO, as they are economically equivalent to the REIT’s Units, with the same features and distribution rights, that are economically equivalent to the distribution received by Unitholders.

“Funds From Operations / Unit” or “FFO / Unit”1 is FFO divided by the issued and outstanding Units, plus Exchangeable Securities (fully diluted basis).

“Gross book value” refers to the total consolidated assets for the IP Portfolio and Total Portfolio.

“Interest Coverage Ratio” or “ICR” covenant refers to a financial metric used to assess a REIT’s ability to meet its interest obligations on outstanding debt. It indicates how many times the operating profit can cover the REIT’s interest expenses over a given period.

“Investments in Joint Ventures” refers to the REIT’s proportionate share of the financial position and results of operation of its investment in joint ventures, which are accounted for using the equity method under IFRS in the consolidated financial statements, are presented below using the proportionate consolidation method at the REIT’s ownership percentage of the related investment. Management views this method as relevant in demonstrating the REIT’s ability to manage the underlying economics of the related investments, including the financial performance and the extent to which the underlying assets are leveraged, which is an important component of risk management.

For the purpose of the proportionate consolidation, the initial investment of both partners in the joint ventures were considered as being equity investments as opposed to a combination of equity and loans and accordingly, the related proportionate consolidation balance sheet items were eliminated as well as the associated finance income and finance costs. As the loans to the joint ventures were considered equity for proportionate consolidation purposes, any impairment recorded on the loans in accordance with IFRS 9 has been reversed for MD&A purposes. As such, any impairment recorded for IFRS purposes results in a difference in equity when reconciling IFRS and proportionate consolidation reporting.

“Investment Properties Portfolio” or “IP Portfolio” refers to the five wholly owned properties of the REIT.

“Net Rental Income” or “NRI” refers to the rental income plus operating cost recoveries income plus other property revenue, less property operating costs and other costs.

“Total Portfolio” refers to the five properties referred to as the IP Portfolio and the five properties of the REIT held in joint-ownership with other parties.

“Weighted average lease break” or “WALB” is a metric used to measure a property portfolio's risk of vacancy and refers to the average period in which all leases in a property or portfolio could expire if tenants exercise their early termination option. It is calculated as the sum of the percentages of rentable area multiplied by the number of years in each remaining lease term before next break option.

“Weighted average lease term” or “WALT” is a metric used to measure a property portfolio’s risk of vacancy and refers to the average period in which all leases in a property or portfolio will expire. It is calculated as the sum of the percentages of rentable area multiplied by the number of years in each remaining lease term.

“Weighted Average number of Units” refers to the mean of periodic values in the number of issued and outstanding Units over a specific reporting period.

data.title: FRMI Stock Clocks Best Day Ever After Report Names Amazon As Project Matador Customer
data.description:
Key points:
  • On Thursday, Fermi said the hyperscaler is advancing an initial 600 MW of power capacity beginning in 2027.
  • No definitive long-term lease has been signed; the customer is committing capital ahead of a lease to secure power within its targeted timeline, the company said.
  • Fermi said it plans to mobilize on site by December 1 and targets initial power in late second quarter or early third quarter of 2027.

Shares of Fermi Inc. (FRMI) extended their rebound on Friday, clocking their best day ever, and building on a sharp Thursday advance after the company disclosed major commitments from an unnamed investment-grade hyperscaler for 600 megawatts of power capacity at its Project Matador campus near Amarillo, Texas.

The Financial Times on Friday reported that people familiar with the matter identified the customer as Amazon, marking a reversal of earlier investment talks that collapsed last December. Amazon is expected to build its own data centers on the site, according to the people cited by the FT.

FRMI shares closed up 26% on Friday on the report.

Hyperscaler Commitments And Site Progress

Fermi is a pre-revenue developer of large-scale AI data-center campuses with dedicated on-site power. Co-founded in early 2025 by former U.S. Energy Secretary Rick Perry and energy financier Toby Neugebauer, it went public in October 2025 with a pitch for the world’s largest such campus.

On Thursday, Fermi said an investment-grade hyperscaler is advancing an initial 600 MW of power capacity at Project Matador beginning in 2027. The customer has agreed to a $200 million prepayment, a $15 million early construction and site-development agreement, and the two sides are finalizing a $90 million purchase of structural steel and building materials Fermi had already secured. No definitive long-term lease has been signed; the company said the customer is committing capital ahead of a lease to secure power within its targeted timeline.

Fermi said it plans to mobilize on site by December 1 and targets initial power in late second quarter or early third quarter of 2027.

FRMI’s Tough Road

FRMI shares have dived from their post-IPO peak amid financing concerns and the collapse of earlier tenant talks, including with Amazon and Oracle. Founder Neugebauer was ousted in April after allegations that his conduct damaged customer relations. Fermi still needs to secure project financing and satisfy conditions on its 99-year land lease with Texas Tech University by year-end, while its air permits face court challenges.

On Thursday, the company reported third-quarter net loss of $141.6 million and said it ended September with $286.3 million in cash against roughly $958 million in debt. It also said that it has terminated its earlier lease with neocloud TensorWave, signed in August.

How Did FRMI Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around FRMI stock jumped from 'bullish' to 'extremely bullish' territory over the past 24 hours, while message volume stayed at 'high' levels.

A Stocktwits user said the deal is “just the beginning” for Fermi.

Another user opined that the deal just “saved the company.”

FRMI stock has dropped 68% year-to-date.
